The film will open against Forgotten Island, a DreamWorks title starring Dave Franco and Jenny Slate, and a re-release of Marvel’s Avengers: Endgame.

Skip to main content

Brad Pitt Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images

Brad Pitt’s Heart of the Beast will sail into theaters on Sept. 25, 2026, Paramount Pictures announced Tuesday.

David Ayer is directing the action-packed survival movie, with J. K. Simmons and Anna Lambe rounding out the cast.

Heart of the Beast centers on a former Army Special Forces soldier (Pitt), who is stranded deep in the Alaskan wilderness with a dog after a plane crash. Ayer directed the project from a script by Cameron Alexander.

Other moments involve the pair facing off with wild animals.

Marty Bowen and Olivia Hamilton are producing alongside Pitt and Ayer (the latter three have a p.g.a. credit). Executive Producers include Damien Chazelle, Cameron Alexander, Chris Long, Pete Chiappetta, Anthony Tittanegro, Andrew Lary, Sophie Cassidy and Zack Conroy.

Company credits include Chazelle and Hamilton’s Wild Chickens Productions, which has a first-look deal with Paramount, Ayer’s Crave Films, Pitt’s Plan B banner and Bowen’s Temple Hill.

Ayer most recently helmed last year’s Jason Statham action vehicle A Working Man and previously directed Pitt in 2014’s Fury. His other features include Suicide Squad, Bright and The Beekeeper.

Pitt led director Joseph Kosinski’s 2025 racing film F1 that picked up four Academy Award nominations and also starred Damson Idris, Kerry Condon and Javier Bardem. Pitt’s other recent credits include Wolfs alongside George Clooney and Chazelle’s 2022 movie, Babylon.

'Cliff Booth' Movie Starring Brad Pitt Takes Over 'Narnia's' Imax Slot This Thanksgiving 'Cliff Booth' Movie Starring Brad Pitt Takes Over 'Narnia's' Imax Slot This Thanksgiving

Cliff Booth is returning to the big screen. “The Adventures of Cliff Booth,” the unofficial title for the sequel to Quentin Tarantino’s “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” will debut in Imax this Thanksgiving.

Netflix has announced the film will get an exclusive two-week run on Imax screens starting Nov. 25. It will land on the streamer on Dec. 23.

“Cliff Booth,” which brings back Brad Pitt in his Oscar-winning role as a longtime stunt-man, is taking the theatrical slot from another high-profile Netflix release, director Greta Gerwig’s “Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew.” Previously set for Thanksgiving 2026, “Narnia” has been delayed to 2027 and will receive a traditional theatrical run — a first for Netflix. Although Netflix appears to be warming to movie theaters, with token releases for “KPop Demon Hunters” and the finale of “Stranger Things,” insiders at the company have stressed there’s no change to its strategy, which prioritizes all things streaming.

Plot details have been kept under wraps, though the logline teases the story takes place in 1977 — “and it’s a very different Hollywood.” That’s after the events of the original, which followed Leonardo DiCaprio and Pitt as aging actor and his longtime stunt double who are struggling to find their place in show biz. “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood,” which paid tribute to the golden age of Hollywood, was set in the late 1960s against the backdrop of the Manson family murders. (Margot Robbie plays Sharon Tate, the up-and-coming actress married to director Roman Polanski, who moves in next door to the boys.)

Brad Pitt Battles Wolves & Wilderness In First Trailer For New Action Thriller Heart Of The Beast

Close

Close

Brad Pitt fights off wolves and the wilderness in the first trailer for his new action thriller movie Heart of the Beast.

Directed by David Ayer, whose best-known work includes End of Watch, Fury, and The Beekeeper, the thrilling survival movie follows Pitt as Special Forces Officer James Belmont, who ends up lost in the Alaskan wilderness with his combat dog, Odin (Uber), after a plane crash. The pair are forced to use their wits and survival skills to find a way out of the hundreds of miles of woodland back to civilization, all while dealing with the mental repercussions of their time in combat.

Now, Paramount Pictures has released a new trailer for Heart of the Beast, revealing what to expect from Pitt's latest film. It reveals Belmont and Odin are camping out in Alaska, even meeting and having a conversation with someone played by J.K. Simmons. Simmons' character warns of how dangerous the area truly is, with the trailer soon cutting to the plane crash that strands its two protagonists. Armed with nothing but the gear they were able to salvage, Belmont embarks on a dangerous journey, all while trying to keep Odin safe. The movie arrives in theaters September 25, 2026.

Check out the full trailer below:

The trailer showcases the many dangers Belmont and Odin will be facing as they traverse the unforgiving wilderness. This includes Pitt's character falling into a rushing river after saving his dog, alongside a swampy landscape the pair trudge through. The end of the trailer sees the duo fighting off a pack of wolves, an event that just might put both of their lives on the line. The wilderness survival movie promises introspection, too, as Pitt's character grapples with what he and Odin went through in wartime.

In addition to Pitt, Uber, and Simmons, the cast also includes Anna Lambe in an undisclosed role. The movie was filmed from March through May 2025 in New Zealand, and was filmed in a multitude of remote locations around the country. It's not Pitt's first time in a survival setting, either. Though more sci-fi, Pitt's space-faring journey in 2019's Ad Astra also saw him alone for much of the time. However, this survivalist setting will clearly be a challenge for his character, but "one last mission" for him and Odin to embark upon.

Brad Pitt and Uber sitting together in Heart of the Beast

The movie is Pitt's first acting role off the back of his critically acclaimed F1, which was released in 2025. It's also one of two movies he'll be starring in this year, with his Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel, The Adventures of Cliff Booth, slated to premiere on Netflix on December 23. However, it promises a deeply emotional movie not just about survival in the wilderness, but also about survival after fighting on the front lines of a war. This personal battle seems to be a thematic element of Belmont and Odin's journey.

With the movie arriving in theaters in just three months, it won't be long before Heart of the Beast showcases the deeply-intertwined bond between Pitt and Uber's characters. Their battle to live is going to be important, but so too will the pair's battle within. As they traverse the wilderness, it remains to be seen how their journey will change them, and what deeper meaning the story will be given.

Brad Pitt filmography

Brad Pitt is an American actor and film producer. His acting career began at age 23 in 1987 with roles in the hit Fox television series 21 Jump Street. He subsequently appeared in episodes for television shows during the late 1980s and played his first major role in The Dark Side of the Sun(1988) the slasher film Cutting Class(1989). He gained recognition in Thelma & Louise(1991), A River Runs Through It(1992), Cool World(1992) and Kalifornia(1993).

He later took on the role of vampire Louis de Pointe du Lac in the horror drama Interview with the Vampire(1994) and for his performance in the epic drama Legends of the Fall(1994), he earned his first Golden Globe Award for Best Actor nomination.

Pitt starred in the David Fincher-directed, commercially successful thriller Seven(1995), in which he played a detective on the trail of a serial killer who murders people he believes are guilty of the seven deadly sins. His performance as a psychotic mental patient in the science fiction film 12 Monkeys won him the Golden Globe Award for Best Supporting Actor and an Academy Award nomination in the same category. He followed it with the role of Heinrich Harrer in the biopic Seven Years in Tibet(1997) and as Death in Meet Joe Black(1998). Pitt reteamed with Fincher to star in the apocalyptic film Fight Club(1999) as anti-consumerist cult leader Tyler Durden, a role that required him to learn boxing, taekwondo, and grappling. A critical and commercial disappointment at the time of release, the film has since developed a cult status. Pitt portrayed Rusty Ryan in the commercially successful heist film series Ocean's Trilogy(2001–07). In 2002, he earned a Primetime Emmy Award nomination for his guest appearance in the sitcom Friends alongside his then-wife Jennifer Aniston. Also that year, Pitt started a production company, Plan B Entertainment, whose first release was the epic war film Troy(2004), starring Pitt. He played an assassin opposite Angelina Jolie in the commercially successful action comedy Mr. & Mrs. Smith(2005).

In 2006, Pitt produced the crime drama The Departed and starred alongside Cate Blanchett in the multi-narrative drama Babel; the former won the Academy Award for Best Picture. Pitt's portrayal of the eponymous man who ages in reverse in the drama The Curious Case of Benjamin Button(2008) earned him an Academy Award for Best Actor nomination. He starred in the successful war film Inglourious Basterds(2009), and produced the superhero film Kick-Ass(2010) and its sequel in 2013. In 2011, he earned critical acclaim for producing and starring in two films—the experimental drama The Tree of Life and the biopic sports drama Moneyball—both of which were nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture. He also garnered a Best Actor nomination for the latter. His biggest commercial success as a leading actor for many years was the apocalyptic film World War Z(2013), which grossed $540 million worldwide. That was only eclipsed by the Apple Studios produced film F1 in 2025. Pitt produced the period drama 12 Years a Slave(2013), for which he won the Academy Award for Best Picture. In 2014, he starred in the war film Fury which received positive reviews from critics and proved to be successful at the box office. For playing a stunt double to Leonardo DiCaprio's character in Quentin Tarantino's film Once Upon a Time in Hollywood(2019), he won an Academy Award, a Golden Globe Award, and a BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role.

Brad Pitt's Long-Awaited Adventure Action Film Sets Release Date

Close

Close

Paramount Pictures has officially set a release date for Heart of the Beast, the newest feature film starring Hollywood icon Brad Pitt. The update comes over two years after director David Ayer signed on to direct, and just under one year since filming on the movie was wrapped.

On Wednesday, it was announced that Heart of the Beast will be released in movie theaters on Sept. 25, 2026 (per Deadline). That puts it against a re-release of Avengers: Endgame and the DreamWorks movie Forgotten Island. Heart of the Beast reunites Pitt and Ayer 12 years after the pair's World War II drama, Fury, was theatrically released. The movie also marks Pitt's first film since he starred in Apple's Oscar-nominated racing drama F1, which was released to great success last summer.

## Brad Pitt and David Ayer Reunite for Heart of the Beast

Directed by Ayer and written by Cameron Alexander, Heart of the Beast stars Pitt as a former Army Special Forces Soldier who's battling for survival alongside his retired combat dog following a plane crash in the Alaskan wilderness. The movie also stars J. K. Simmons (Oz, Spider-Man) and Anna Lambe (North of North, True Detective: Night Country).

"All I can say is it's just going to be a classic old-school adventure movie,” Ayer told Collider about the film last year. "This is what Hollywood excelled at for decades, and I want to bring that cinematic tradition back and just adventure storytelling."

Ayer and Pitt are serving as producers on Heart of the Beast alongside Olivia Hamilton and Marty Bowen. Executive producers include Damien Chazelle, Scott Lumpkin, Cameron Alexander, Chris Long, Pete Chiapetta, Anthony Tittanegro, Andrew Lary, Sophie Cassidy, and Zack Conroy.

## Fans Also Await Brad Pitt's Other Upcoming Films

Cliff Booth drives to pick up Rick in Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.Image via Sony Pictures

There are other movies in development for fans of Pitt to anticipate. He is reprising his role from 2019's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood for an upcoming sequel, director David Fincher's The Adventures of Cliff Booth, which is set to be released on Netflix later this year. While he's not directing, Once Upon a Time in Hollywood helmer Quentin Tarantino penned the screenplay. Elizabeth Debicki, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, and Carla Gugino also appear in the film, which has a reported budget of around $200 million.

Pitt is also set to star in Edward Berger's The Riders, an upcoming psychological thriller also starring Julianne Nicholson and Michael Smiley. In that movie, Pitt plays a family man who searches across Europe for answers after his wife mysteriously disappears. The film is based on the original 1994 novel by Tim Winton. Along with starring, Pitt is also serving as a producer on the project under his Plan B Entertainment banner. A release date has not yet been set.

Heart of the Beast will be released in movie theaters on Sept. 25, 2026.

Brad Pitt‘s Heart of the Beast trailer got pulses racing at CinemaCon.

Paramount Pictures is set to release director David Ayer‘s film in theaters, and the first trailer debuted at the Las Vegas event. J. K. Simmons and Anna Lambe round out the cast.

Heart of the Beast centers on a former Army Special Forces soldier (Pitt), who fights for survival with his combat dog after a plane crash strands them in the Alaskan wilderness. Ayer directed the project from a script by Cameron Alexander.

https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/shrek-5-trailer-gingerbread-man-mike-myers-sequel-1236623220/

The trailer focuses on the bond between Pitt and his pooch. “I’m gonna get you home,” Pitt assures the canine after their plane crashes. “We’re just going to have to do this the hard way.”

This footage also teases a frightening moment when Pitt and his dog cross a river, and Pitt’s effort to keep his dog from falling leads himself to wind up in the water. Other moments involve the pair facing off with wild animals.

“One last mission,” Pitt says. “I’m not going to let you die out here.”

Producers include Damien Chazelle and Olivia Hamilton for their Wild Chickens Productions banner through its first-look deal with Paramount. Also producing are Temple Hill Entertainment, Ayer for Crave Films and Pitt for Plan B. Richard Raymond serves as co-producer.

Ayer most recently helmed last year’s Jason Statham action vehicle A Working Man and previously directed Pitt in 2014’s Fury. His other features include Suicide Squad, Bright and The Beekeeper.

Pitt led director Joseph Kosinski’s 2025 racing film F1 that picked up four Academy Award nominations and also starred Damson Idris, Kerry Condon and Javier Bardem. Pitt’s other recent credits include Wolfs alongside George Clooney and Chazelle’s 2022 movie, Babylon.
